reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational concept of perception-time dynamics establishes a temporal framework for understanding how sensory data is processed and interpreted. This is modeled as a stochastic process where t_p represents the duration of perception, bounded by neural latency and cognitive capacity. In GSI, this translates into Bayesian inference over time-series data, where prior beliefs about perception evolve with new evidence. The retinal involvement hypothesis introduces a critical variable—after-images—which suggest that even in hallucinations, retinal structures may be activated. This implies a dual pathway: one involving direct sensory input and another involving internal neural generation. Hallucination background obscuration further complicates this by introducing opacity effects that mask real-world inputs. These primitives form a coherent system where perception is not merely a passive reception but an active construction shaped by both external stimuli and internal states. The interplay between these elements creates a complex feedback loop in GSE’s situational reasoning engine, while GSI uses them to refine probabilistic models of reality versus illusion.
